\title{Normalized Nonlinear Comparison on Dependency-Safe Local Cylinders}

\begin{abstract}
We replace a high-dimensional global chart ball by an intersection of local
four-link cylinders.  A normalized restriction theorem converts local
oscillation and reference-complement estimates into an explicit density
comparison.  At the frozen centered $SU(2)$ reference the loss is
$3.02\cdot10^{-5}$ per support unit, closing that finite normalization gate.
Uniformity over retained nonlinear boundary states remains open.
\end{abstract}

\section{Restriction theorem}
Let $\nu_s$ be a reference probability law, $G_s$ a measurable good set, and
\[
 \mu_{s,G}(A)=
 \frac{\int_{A\cap G_s}e^{-R_s}\,d\nu_s}
      {\int_{G_s}e^{-R_s}\,d\nu_s}.
\]

\begin{theorem}
Suppose, uniformly in the retained state $s$,
\[
 \nu_s(G_s)\ge 1-\delta,
 \qquad \operatorname{osc}_{G_s}R_s\le m\kappa,
 \qquad 0\le\delta<1.
\]
Then every measurable $A$ satisfies
\[
 \mu_{s,G}(A)
 \le \frac{e^{m\kappa}}{1-\delta}\,\nu_s(A).
\]
The logarithmic comparison loss per support unit is
\[
 \kappa-\frac1m\log(1-\delta).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
On $G_s$, divide the numerator and denominator by
$e^{-\inf_{G_s}R_s}$.  The numerator is at most $\nu_s(A\cap G_s)$,
while the denominator is at least
$e^{-\operatorname{osc}_{G_s}R_s}\nu_s(G_s)$.  Insert the two hypotheses.
\end{proof}

If $R_s$ is a sum of $m$ local terms, each based on a radius-$r$ cylinder,
with vanishing value and gradient at its center and Hessian remainder at most
$H$, then one may take $\kappa=Hr^2$.

\section{Frozen-reference calibration}
Stages 21 and 22 provide
\[
 m=216,\quad r=0.006023157807602598,\quad
 \delta\le0.002792708080357906,
 \quad H=0.4746710865657404.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 Hr^2=1.72203218\cdot10^{-5},\qquad
 \frac{mHr^2-\log(1-\delta)}m
 =3.01676133\cdot10^{-5}.
\]
This is far below the declared target $0.2$.  The global $408$-dimensional
ball used previously was therefore a representation mismatch: the relevant
coverage event is local and overlapping, not a small Euclidean ball in every
physical coordinate simultaneously.

\section{Frontier}
The theorem is uniform whenever its two hypotheses are uniform.  The present
calibration establishes them for the frozen centered reference, but not for
every positive-mass retained nonlinear $SU(2)$ state.  Nor does a restricted
good-channel comparison control the bad partition.  Those two quantifiers
remain the physical frontier; no full-measure, RG, continuum, or mass-gap
claim follows.
